reason: Pinned §2.1 supports clarifying string equality, but §9 already defines model hashing and the repository contains verifier-side vectors, weakening the broader claims.
The missing retention floor is real, but §7.3 already requires insertion and retention only through the first action cannot guarantee the proposed second-run replay denial.
Sections 7.3 and 8 already establish nonce-only identity, leaving useful issuer-variation and duplicate-list coverage gaps rather than the claimed undefined uniqueness rule.

Section 7.2 omits request-delivery failures and the pinned reference host swallows stdin errors, supporting an early-close allow vector despite the incorrect claim that bounded reading necessarily requires early exit.
Pinned §7.2 unconditionally rejects signal death, while the existing signal fixture emits no verdict, confirming a bounded additive vector that catches stdout-first fail-open handling.
Section 3.2 already requires reserving every present entry, while both pinned reference hosts ignore the list in local mode, supporting a conformance gap and conflicting-prose clarification.

The absent retention floor is confirmed, but rejecting currently valid verdicts requires a compatibility decision, relational validation beyond exclusiveMinimum, and controlled timing for the one-second replay case.
Empty strings are schema-valid and the reference store discards blank lines on reload, but skipping entries already violates §3.2 and adding minLength requires a compatibility decision.
The closed allow shape is verified and §11 permits optional-field evolution, but provenance logging remains an extension proposal without a demonstrated authorization or interoperability defect.

Fixtures do not validate forwarded request schemas, but positive controls already require stdin EOF, so Tier 2 should add schema-validating positive controls and discard the proposed expected-deny EOF case.
Live [issue #1835](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/issues/1835) is closed and khandrew1 is held, requiring terminal treatment for this issue-based opportunity and the channel cap.

The [repository](https://github.com/aerf-spec/agentmint-python) confirms signed receipts and AERF v0.1 but describes stability as intended before 1.0, with limited adoption evidence and overlap primarily in receipts.
The pinned IANA section already specifies Specification Required, registry fields, initial contents, and wire-major reconciliation while explicitly declining a kind registry.
Pinned Appendix B explicitly disclaims normative wire obligations and binding v2 permits only six ASCII-named fields, invalidating the claimed draft blocker and proposed non-ASCII-key counterexample.
The pinned draft pseudocode omits schema validation and signal/output-bound handling and checks nonzero exit before timeout, supporting a bounded rewrite aligned with the normative obligations.

The historical listing accurately identifies set 0.5.0 and [RFC 7942](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7942#section-2) makes fields advisory, while prior files already record 27/28 and this proposal lacks a runnable HUT command.

Microsoft's [AGT documentation](https://developer.microsoft.com/blog/securing-mcp-a-control-plane-for-agent-tool-execution/) confirms substantial enforcement overlap and multiple policy backends, but EVC interoperability remains untested and the card must remain stale until required GitHub API reconciliation succeeds.

[Datatracker](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-daniel-ai-agent-internet-architecture/) now lists revision -03, making the -00 framing stale, while this individual architecture draft offers positioning value without demonstrated competing enforcement or WG adoption.

[Issue #1166](https://github.com/VoltAgent/voltagent/issues/1166) remains open and describes a compatible pre-action seam, but it is an APort/OAP proposal without verified maintainer commitment to EVC.

Live [issue #1835](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/issues/1835) is closed, the engagement graph records the middleware seam as already merged, and the held maintainer requires channel_state capped at 5.

The proposed local Cargo build writes outside standards-autoresearch, violating rule 2a, while commands omit the host_behavior filter and ordinary runner output lacks successful per-vector failure_class values.

The empty ledger warrants curating this evidence, but prior experiment outputs already record 27/28 at 17642a5 and reproduction requires a pinned HUT adapter rather than the nonexistent README command.

A coverage map is valuable, but the proposed grep and fixture glob miss obligations and actual vector definitions, while EOF and classification assertions already exist and §16.5 documents the ordering limitation.

Read-only sync:check confirms 31 vendored files plus MANIFEST, supporting a registry record that includes vendor/test-vectors.json and normalized tarball comparisons instead of treating fixture scripts as vector definitions.
